novelty.justification: The claim's novelty route is primarily a new causal measurement and attribution method, namely the proposed “Binding Ledger” that assigns each failure to a “concept-stage or a binding-stage cause,” rather than a wholly new shared-concept phenomenon. The closest prior work is “When Meanings Meet: Investigating the Emergence and Quality of Shared Concept Spaces during Multilingual Language Model Training,” which uses causal activation patching and reports language-dependent alignment and misleading behavioral shifts, while “Multilingual Contrastive Decoding via Language-Agnostic Layers Skipping” studies late/early language mismatch and inference-time layer interventions; searches used “multilingual concept space activation patching,” “language re-binding failure multilingual reasoning,” “per-failure causal attribution cross-lingual,” “late-layer language vector steering,” and “multilingual reasoning language mismatch.” Moving from these works to the claim is a substantive but natural methodological extension: it combines existing patching and language-vector interventions into a per-failure double-dissociation ledger, rather than introducing a fundamentally new causal principle or paradigm, so the contribution is above a direct transfer but remains mainly a non-trivial operationalization and integration.
